portInfo.description: Marigot is the main town on the French collectivity of Saint-Martin in the northeast Caribbean. It is not the same call as Philipsburg on Dutch Sint Maarten—confirm your itinerary lists Marigot or Saint-Martin on the French side. The Établissement Portuaire de Saint-Martin (Port of Saint-Martin) handles cruise ships through anchorage and tender landings, with the ferry terminal and Marina Fort Louis on the Marigot waterfront.
portInfo.location: Baie de la Potence / Galisbay, Saint-Martin (French side of the island shared with Sint Maarten)
portInfo.language: French; English widely used in tourism and shops
portInfo.currency: Euro (EUR); US dollars are often accepted—confirm change policies ashore

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Confirm your sailing's arrival details: Marigot calls use anchorage and tender landings coordinated by the Port of Saint-Martin, not the large Philipsburg cruise piers on the Dutch side. Follow gangway and tender instructions from your ship each day.
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Port of Saint-Martin public information cites about 10 minutes from central Marigot after cruise landings; tender location and crowds change that in practice.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Port of Saint-Martin public information cites about 10 minutes from central Marigot after cruise landings; tender location and crowds change that in practice.
gettingThere.walkingTime: From many landings, the Marigot waterfront and lower town are often walkable if you are mobile—Fort Louis adds a steep uphill segment.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Taxis and informal transport serve Marigot; agree on destination and return timing, and keep payment options your driver accepts.
gettingThere.publicTransport: There is no standard cruise-shuttle contract—use ship tenders first. Trips toward Philipsburg or Dutch-side beaches involve border crossing and separate transport planning.

thingsToDo.intro: A Marigot call is usually a compact French-side day: harbour front, shopping streets, and Fort Louis views—unless your ship sells a Dutch-side or island-wide excursion instead.
topThings: Marigot shops / cafés opposite the terminal.
Island tours — coach; confirm French-side vs Dutch-side drop-offs.
Marigot waterfront and harbour promenade near the ferry terminal
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Confirm your sailing's arrival details before booking independent transport. All-aboard time matters more than map distance on tender days.
